name: IllumiNeuro Protocol
lead: IllumiNeuro Protocol is a multi-peptide nootropic blend sold by research-peptide vendors for memory, focus and stress resilience. People who buy blends like this hope for sharper concentration, calmer mood and better sleep-wake regulation, which they connect to a more energetic, composed presence and consistent work on their appearance goals.[1]

One database lists the components as PE-22-28, Pinealon, NA-Semax Amidate and NA-Selank Amidate, though other sellers describe different vial contents and amounts.[1] It is marketed for memory, focus, learning, neuroprotection, anxiety reduction, mood support and circadian support, mostly by subcutaneous injection, with intranasal use also mentioned.[1] The database ties anxiety relief mainly to the Selank component and BDNF-related effects to the Semax component, and calls many of the claimed benefits theoretical.[1]

The two best-known parent peptides have a Russian origin. Semax is a heptapeptide analogue of a fragment of ACTH, first described in the literature in 1991 and a prescription drug in Russia, and Selank is a seven-amino-acid analogue of the immune peptide tuftsin developed at the Institute of Molecular Genetics of the Russian Academy of Sciences.[2][3] The combination itself has not been studied in clinical trials.

paras: The vendor database lists a four-peptide mix: PE-22-28, Pinealon, NA-Semax Amidate and NA-Selank Amidate.[1] Claimed benefits include memory, focus, neuroprotection, anxiety relief, mood, neurite outgrowth and sleep-wake regulation, which the listing itself describes as largely theoretical.[1]

Wikipedia describes Semax as a synthetic heptapeptide analogue of an ACTH fragment, first described in 1991, used in Russia for stroke, transient ischemic attack, cognitive disorders, peptic ulcers and optic nerve disease, and sold online elsewhere as a nootropic.[2] Its exact mechanism is unknown; animal studies report raised hippocampal BDNF and antidepressant-like and anxiolytic-like effects.[2] In the United States it is not FDA approved and is unscheduled.[2]

Selank is described as a 'nootropic anxiolytic' that is a synthetic analogue of tuftsin, with clinical studies examining cognition and anxiety, including comparisons with benzodiazepines, and rat studies reporting effects on monoamines, serotonin metabolism and hippocampal BDNF.[3] Wikipedia notes both drugs are available in Russian and Ukrainian pharmacies.[3]

The listing names mild injection-site reactions, nasal irritation with intranasal use, vivid dreams and initial headache as reported side effects, and lists bipolar disorder or psychosis, pregnancy or breastfeeding, and seizure disorders (a theoretical concern) as cautions.[1] It also notes possible batch variability in the four-component formulation and the research-only status of the product.[1]

No studies found on this four-peptide combination. The database states that no clinical studies exist on it and that human efficacy data for the individual components are limited.[1] Clinical and animal work exists for Semax and Selank individually, as summarised in their encyclopedia entries.[2][3]

timeline.event: Semax is first described in the scientific literature.[2]

card.summary: A vendor-sold four-peptide nootropic blend marketed for memory, focus and stress resilience, aimed at sharper mental performance.
card.note: Research-labeled product; no clinical studies of the combination and contents vary by seller.

quick.overview:
IllumiNeuro Protocol is a research-peptide blend sold by vendors as a nootropic. One database lists its contents as PE-22-28, Pinealon, NA-Semax Amidate and NA-Selank Amidate in a single vial [1].

It is marketed for memory, focus, learning, stress resilience and mood support, typically by subcutaneous injection and sometimes intranasally [1].
quick.mechanism: The blend combines peptides associated with different roles: Semax-type peptides for focus and memory, Selank-type for stress and anxiety, and others listed for neuroprotection and circadian support [1].
quick.risks: The listing says it is not approved for human use and that no clinical studies exist on this four-peptide combination [1]. Listed side effects include injection-site reactions, nasal irritation, vivid dreams and headache; listed cautions include bipolar disorder, psychosis, pregnancy and seizure disorders, and batch variability is noted [1].
